_comment: Ships trade: they buy a commodity at one port and sell it at the next (see data/markets.json, where ships also buy their own fuel at a price that follows the local oil price). starting_money covers a first ship and its first cargo. Breakdowns (from company level min_company_level): every interval_s seconds, each ship at sea (not recovery boats) rolls its own chance of losing hit of its maintenance (0.5 = 50 points). The chance runs from chance_at_full at 100% maintenance to chance_at_empty at 0%, times the model's breakdown_factor (bigger ships are sturdier), times an age factor (1 + age_per_hour_at_sea for each hour the ship has spent at sea, up to max_age_factor), less the durability skill. initial_view_width_deg: how many degrees of longitude the map shows across when it opens, centered on the home port.
_company_colors_comment: Colors a new company can choose (its name in the top bar and the rings around its HQ and hubs): [id, name, hex], in picker order.
_weather_comment: Storms (scripts/sim/weather.gd), for saves founded with Moderate or Harsh storms. From company level min_company_level they slow ships, wear them and make breakdowns likelier, and the strongest hurricane, typhoon and cyclone cores close ports; before that (and in saves without storms) nothing happens to ships, though storms are still drawn. levels: slow is the most a storm's core cuts speed (fuel per mile stays the same, so a storm alone can't strand a ship), wear the most it multiplies wear and breakdown chance, close_at how strong a tropical storm must be over a port to close it (0..1), rate how many storms form, times the basins' per_year. Each basin forms storms of its kind in its months (1-12; peak months twice as often), per_year a year on average, somewhere in spawn ([[lon min, lon max], [lat min, lat max]]), with a radius_nm of effect, lasting life_days (a calendar day is 72 s of play), moving speed_nm calendar nm an hour (about knots). Tropical kinds (hurricane, typhoon, cyclone) drift west and poleward, then curve away east past recurve_lat; gales run east. names are used in turn.
_calendar_comment: The in-game calendar starts at start (UTC) and runs minutes_per_second calendar minutes per second of play at 1x, matched to real ship speeds: a Scooter's 5.44 nm a second is about 16 knots, so Rome to Tunis takes about 20 hours on the calendar and Shanghai to Rotterdam about a month.
_rough_seas_comment: Rough seas far south: ships wear wear_factor times as fast south of lat, and cargo on legs to or from a port south of it sells for pay_bonus more. upper_lakes_bonus: cargo on legs between two ports on the upper Great Lakes (Superior, Michigan, Huron: ports.json lake) sells for that much more, like the real ore and grain trade.
_harbor_speed_comment: Ships ease out of port and into the next: leaving, a ship builds up from start x its speed to full speed over about seconds of sailing (steady acceleration), and arriving it slows the same way, in steps pieces each (the zones fuel, range and arrival times are worked out over, like the convoy canals). On a leg too short for both, each takes half of it.
_xp_comment: XP: every delivery (when unloading finishes) gives the company and the ship XP for the work done: units x leg distance x xp_per_container_nm, weighted by the commodity's base price against markets.json xp_ref_price (whatever it sold for). Company levels run 1 to max_company_level. Level L costs (company_level_minutes[0] + company_level_minutes[1] x (L - 1)) minutes of the XP a full fleet at that level would earn at sea (at_sea_share of the time): every unlocked cargo model with all the slots it has at that level. So each level takes about as long no matter how big the fleet has become, and level 100 takes about 20 hours. ship_slots: how many of each model you can own. [start, every]: a model gets start slots when it unlocks and one more every that many company levels (or every slot_every levels, if the model sets it in ship_models.json), up to its max_owned. cargo is container ships and gas tankers, recovery is recovery boats. Ships level 0 to ship_max_level, one skill point per level; see ship_models.json xp_first_level and ship_level_growth. skills: the bonus per skill level (speed: top speed +2%; durability: wear and breakdown chance -5%; efficiency: fuel burn -3%), up to skill_max_level each. skill_costs: each skill level also costs money, first x the model's price for a skill's 1st level plus step more for each level it already has (10%, 15% ... 55% for the 10th), each skill priced separately.
_mega_comment: Mega upgrade: once a model has max_owned ships, all at ship_max_level, it can be bought once for cost_factor x the model's price (Scooter 20: $1,000,000). Every ship of that model then gets speed_bonus more top speed and profit_bonus more profit on each profitable trade (recovery boats: speed_bonus more top speed and recovery_fuel_saving less fuel burn). recovery_xp: a recovery boat earns per_nm XP for every mile of a finished recovery job (out to the lost ship and carrying it to port), and the company earns company_share of the XP the rescued ship's full hold would earn over the miles it was carried. Not for recovery boats.
_port_sizes_comment: Port sizes run 1 to max: bands are [name, smallest size] (Small 1-25, Medium 26-50, Large 51-75, Giant 76-100); ports.json size is where each starts. A port grows by the cargo value the player's ships load and unload there: value / (growth_value_per_point x its size) points (bigger ports need more), banked up to max_pending and applied at up to max_growth_per_hour. Tuned so a mid-game company's busiest port (about $60M an hour through a size-50 port) climbs a band in about 15 hours, and no port faster than a band in 5 hours. From company level shrink_from_level, a port above shrink_floor loses shrink_per_hour (a band in about 30 hours), less whatever it grows, never going below shrink_floor. Sizes in the normal range play as before sizes; toward size 1 the player's trades move prices up to impact_at_min times as much (and their effect lasts that much longer) and fuel and repairs cost costs_at_min more, and toward max impact_at_max and costs_at_max. ship_models.json min_port is the smallest band a model can dock at.
_hubs_comment: Headquarters and hubs: the HQ is at the home port from the start; one more hub every every_company_levels company levels, up to max_hubs, each placed for good at any port. A hub earns the XP of every delivery unloaded at its port and levels 0 to max_level; level L to L+1 costs (level_minutes[0] + level_minutes[1] x L) minutes of traffic_share of a full fleet's XP at the current company level, so a hub taking about a quarter of the fleet's deliveries maxes out in about 6 hours. Each level is an upgrade point for 4 paths of up to max_path_level points, and spending one costs upgrade_cost plus upgrade_cost_step for each point already in that path (2M, 2.5M, 3M...); per_point is each point's bonus to every ship docking there (xp: ship XP, costs: fuel and repair prices, speed: port stop time, pay: the price cargo sells for there). Every delivery unloaded at a hub also earns the company more XP: company_xp_base plus company_xp_per_10_levels for every 10 hub levels (+10% at level 0, +50% at level 40). The HQ's bonuses, this one included, are hq_multiplier times a hub's.
